```text
38:- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
94:| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
95:| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
97:> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
123:> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
262:The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.
336:- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.

```text
# Session/workspace switcher cable channel for herdr (tv) — sesh analog
#
# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
#
# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.

[metadata]
name = "herdr-sesh"
description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]

[source]
command = [
  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
]
display = "{split:\t:2}"
output = "{split:\t:1}"

[preview]
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
case "$kind" in
  ws)
    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    ;;
  dir)
    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
    ;;
esac
'''

[ui]
input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"
ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]

[actions.open]
description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
case "$kind" in
  ws)  herdr workspace focus "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  dir) herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
esac
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_ws]
description = "Close the selected herdr workspace"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ "$kind" = "ws" ] && [ -n "$ref" ] && herdr workspace close "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"
```
</details></tool-use>

#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
#
# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
# new contents on stdout.
#
# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
#
# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
# round-trips both.
#
# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
set -eu

tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM

cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
TOML

live=$(cat)

if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  set -- python3 -
else
  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
  cat "$tmpl_file"
  exit 0
fi

HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit_template():
    sys.stdout.write(template_text)


# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
        emit_template()
        sys.exit(0)

# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    emit_template()
    sys.exit(0)

MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}

live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}

# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
        continue
    doc[key] = value

sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
PYEOF
```

```text
# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator.
#
# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or
# nest deliberately; see docs/tools/herdr.md "nested inside tmux"). Nothing here
# touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
# Full feasibility matrix + behavior model + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
#
# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = true            # follow OS light/dark
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true

[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
# cwd — same as a split. herdr issue #912 changed `follow` so tabs behave like
# splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root" was treated as a bug and
# removed. NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for
# that use the prefix+C command below (derives the space root → tab create --cwd).
# See docs/tools/herdr.md.
new_cwd = "follow"

# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)

# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)

# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the
# navigate-mode-only movement keys. Add vim j/k alongside the default arrows so
# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]

# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

# btop / nvtop monitors as floating command panes (same mechanism as lazygit —
# a real PTY that closes when you quit the tool). Quick Actions can't host these:
# herdr-plus runs an action via `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin, so an interactive TUI
# either exits immediately (btop) or can't receive function keys like F10 (nvtop).
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+M"
type = "pane"
command = "btop"
description = "btop system monitor (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+N"
type = "pane"
command = "nvtop"
description = "nvtop GPU monitor (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+`"
type = "pane"
command = "$SHELL"
description = "scratch shell (popup pane)"

# --- New tab at the workspace ("space") root dir (prefix+C) ---
# herdr's native new-tab (prefix+c) and the mouse "+" button follow new_cwd,
# which on herdr >=0.7.x means the FOCUSED pane's live cwd (issue #912 made
# `follow` treat new tabs like splits). This binding instead opens a new tab at
# the workspace ROOT dir — the lowest-numbered tab's pane cwd, i.e. what herdr
# uses for the space label. No new_cwd value does this; the helper derives it
# (herdr workspace get has no cwd field). prefix+c stays = follow-focused-pane.
# Only affects THIS key; the mouse "+" button can't be intercepted.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+C"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+U"
type = "pane"
command = "tv tools"
description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"

# URL picker (tmux prefix+u analog — joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads the focused
# pane, fzf-picks a URL (same rewrites: http(s)/ftp/file, www., IP, git@ remote,
# quoted owner/repo, npm import), opens it via the repo's cross-platform `x open`.
# Visible screen by default; `url-pick.sh --source recent` scans full scrollback.
# Kept beside prefix+U so the u/U pair sits together. Helper mirrors pane-copy.sh.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+T"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-sesh"
description = "Session / workspace / dir switcher (herdr-aware tv channel)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+a"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live agent panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+f"
type = "pane"
command = "tv fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts SSH picker (tv)"

# --- Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ---
# prefix+m toggles a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag (herdr
# custom-status, orthogonal to agent state — survives the pane going idle when
# you peek in). prefix+i opens the flagged-panes inbox. Uses $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
# (the keybind-context var; NOT the ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID). Logic lives in
# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh; see docs/tools/herdr.md.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+m"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh toggle \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+i"
type = "pane"
command = "tv herdr-review"
description = "Review-pending inbox — flagged panes (herdr-aware tv channel)"

# --- Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (prefix+P/D/V/S) ---
# One helper (~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh) distills a pane's data and pipes it to
# `x copy`. Bound to the KEYBIND-context $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the pane focused
# when the key was pressed; the helper falls back to `herdr pane current` if empty).
# The SAME four ops are also herdr-plus Quick Actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/
# config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/). Uppercase letters resolve to
# prefix+shift+<letter>; P/D/V/S avoid herdr's reserved shift builtins (shift+H/J/K/L
# swap-pane) and this repo's own shift+B (new_worktree) / shift+R (reload). Confirm
# clean with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+P"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh process \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "copy pane process info"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+D"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh coord \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "copy pane coordinate (session>space>tab>pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+V"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh content \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\" --source visible"
description = "copy pane content (visible screen)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+S"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh content \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\" --source recent"
description = "copy pane content (full scrollback)"

# Copy a file PATH from the pane (extrakto-style, herdr side). Extracts path-like
# tokens; two-tier: paths that EXIST under the pane cwd (copied as resolved
# absolute) on top, unverified candidates below a separator. fzf-pick → `x copy`.
# Lowercase p pairs with the uppercase copy family (P/D/V/S), same u/U convention.
# Passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD for the existence check. Helper mirrors pane-copy.sh.
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+p"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\" --cwd \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\""
description = "copy a file path from the pane (fzf, two-tier)"

# --- herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + popup-menu analog) ---
# Requires: herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus
# Projects = declarative multi-pane workspace templates (see
# dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/).
# Quick Actions = fuzzy command launcher. If the plugin is not installed these
# bindings simply no-op.

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+O"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects"
description = "herdr-plus: Projects (layout launcher)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+y"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"
```

```text
38:- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
93:| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
104:| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
123:> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
335:- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read herdr-agent-panes channel

`cat dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`

```text
# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
#
# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
#
# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_pane]
description = "Close the pane (confirm prompt)"
command = '''
p='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$p" ] && exit 0
printf 'Close pane %s? [y/N] ' "$p"
read -r ans
case "$ans" in
  y|Y|yes|YES) herdr pane close "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "closed $p" || echo "failed (already gone?)" ;;
  *) echo "aborted" ;;
esac
echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
'''
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_dir]
description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:4}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"
```
</details></tool-use>

# Goto picker: option to limit tree depth (workspaces/tabs only, hide panes) [CLOSED]

## Feature request

The goto picker (`prefix+g`) always renders the full tree down to individual panes. When you mainly use it to jump between workspaces and tabs, the pane rows add noise and make the list longer to scan (e.g. every tab shows an extra "pane N" child even for single-pane tabs).

Proposal: a config option to cap the tree depth, e.g.

```toml
[ui]
goto_depth = "tab"   # "workspace" | "tab" | "pane" (default: "pane")
```

or alternatively collapse pane rows by default with `l`/`right` to expand a tab on demand.

Use case: with one workspace per repo and a handful of named tabs (agent / lazygit / editor), workspace→tab is the granularity I navigate at 95% of the time.

# Goto picker: allow vim-style 'l' (and 'h') alongside Enter to switch [CLOSED]

## Feature request

In the goto picker (`prefix+g`), the only way to confirm/switch to the highlighted node is `enter`. Since `j/k` already work for moving up/down the tree, it would feel natural for vim users to also support:

- `l` → switch to (or expand) the highlighted workspace/tab/pane
- `h` → collapse the highlighted node (optional, for symmetry)

This would make the whole picker navigable with the home-row `hjkl` cluster: `j/k` to move, `l` to dive/confirm, `h` to back out — matching the muscle memory of vim, yazi, and similar tree UIs.

Currently these picker-internal keys appear to be hardcoded (no `[keys]` options for them), so either hardcoding `l`/`h` as aliases or exposing them as configurable bindings would both solve it.

Thanks for herdr — the goto picker is already my main way of moving between spaces!

```text
# Changelog

## Unreleased

## [0.7.5] - 2026-07-21

### Breaking Changes
- Installed and linked plugins, including their enabled state, are now global to the current user instead of isolated by Herdr session. Plugins installed only in a named session on Herdr 0.7.3 must be installed or linked again. (#1174)

### Added
- Added a live-agent CLI facade with named `start`, atomic `prompt`, logical `send-keys`, and server-owned `wait` workflows. Agent startup targets an existing pane without changing topology, validates the requested interactive agent kind and strict agent name, and accepts native arguments after `--`.
- Added transient declarative Agent view queries through `agent.view.set/clear`; filtered and sorted views now define sidebar, mobile, mouse, and agent-keybind navigation order.
- Added one-shot plugin `[[startup]]` hooks for restoring plugin-owned state after server startup and live handoff.
- Added per-token foreground, bold, and dim styling to expanded Space and Agent sidebar row layouts.
- Added `ui.sidebar_start_collapsed` to launch Herdr with the sidebar collapsed. (#1463)
- Added `ui.prompt_new_workspace_name` to ask for a workspace name before interactive TUI creation.
- Added macOS support for the `HERDR_AGENT=<agent>` foreground-process hint, allowing agents hidden behind host-visible wrappers such as `nono` to use the named agent's screen manifest. (#679)

### Changed
- Agent commands now accept only a unique live agent name or the pane ID currently hosting that agent. Names are cleared when the occupant exits, is released, or is replaced. The old top-level `wait` commands were replaced by `agent wait` and `pane wait-output`, and `agent send` was replaced by `agent send-keys`.
- The session navigator now uses connected tree glyphs, groups matches by workspace, and automatically selects the first result when a search begins. (#1611)

### Fixed
- CLI requests now return a machine-readable `protocol_mismatch` error when the client and server protocols differ, while recovery commands remain available. (#1435)
- Linux sound notifications now terminate and reap audio players that do not exit, preventing unavailable audio from leaving CPU-bound `mpg123` processes behind. (#1622)
- Oversized bracketed text pastes are now rejected with a client-local notification instead of disconnecting the client. (#1665)
- Agent prompt waits now report `agent_prompt_stalled` after five seconds without an observed state change instead of waiting indefinitely after an ineffective submission.
- `herdr config check` now reports unknown config keys with their full paths instead of treating ignored typos as valid configuration. (#1573)
- Codex panes with customized static terminal titles now fall back to the live working footer instead of remaining idle, while OSC activity remains preferred. (#1563)
- Grok panes now preserve working and blocked state from terminal signals and pinned background-work status instead of falling back to idle mid-turn.
- OpenCode lifecycle reports are now serialized so out-of-order plugin events cannot leave an idle pane marked working. (#1519)
- Kimi question prompts now report blocked until the user answers or dismisses them.
- Pi lifecycle reporting now uses settled events, preventing transient message boundaries from publishing an idle state mid-turn.
- The Pi, OMP, OpenCode, and Kilo Code integrations can now be installed on Windows and report lifecycle state and native session identity through Herdr's named-pipe API. (#1531)
- Named agent prompts now honor live bracketed-paste mode before sending Enter, preserving OpenCode text such as `A != B` instead of triggering shell mode. (#1525)
- New panes, tabs, layouts, and workspaces using `new_cwd = "follow"` now inherit the foreground process-group leader's working directory instead of an unrelated helper process directory. (#1472)
- Cached pane working directories no longer trigger repeated filesystem checks, avoiding slow sidebar rendering on network filesystems such as Ceph. (#1603)
- Windows foreground-process snapshots are now shared across panes, reducing idle CPU use in sessions with many panes. (#1158)
- Terminal diff streams now batch contiguous writes, reducing the visible wave effect while scrolling pane history. (#283)
- A standalone Escape arriving beside another key is now preserved as its own input instead of being combined into a fabricated Alt chord. (#541)
```

Most importantly, this repo includes its own sesh-like quick jump (`prefix + T` → `tv herdr-sesh`) that lists workspaces alongside zoxide frecency directories, lets you jump to or create new workspaces at specific directories, and can close workspaces with Ctrl+D.

For expand/collapse: you can collapse individual spaces with Space while in the navigator, but there's no global collapse-all or expand-all feature. 研究完了，直接回答三個問題。

## 1. 有沒有 Cmd+K 式的 space 搜尋跳轉？有，而且你這台已經有四個入口

| 鍵 | 是什麼 | 粒度 |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix + g` | herdr 原生 **session navigator**（你截圖那個） | space → tab → pane 全樹 |
| `prefix + w` | workspace navigator（sidebar navigate mode，本 repo 把 `navigate_workspace_up/down` 加了 `j`/`k`） | **只有 space 層** |
| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` — 本 repo 自己寫的 **sesh 類比** | **扁平 space 清單** |
| `prefix + a` / `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-agent-panes`（跳到跑 agent 的 pane）/ `tv herdr-review`（⭐ 待審 inbox） | pane |

`prefix + T` 才是真正的 sesh 對應物：它比原生 goto 多一件事 —— 除了切換既有 space，還能從 **zoxide frecency 目錄直接開新 space**（`herdr workspace create --cwd`），`Ctrl+D` 關掉 space。定義在 `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`，綁定在 `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`。

## 2. 展開/收起：有隱藏鍵，但**沒有** expand-all / collapse-all

`prefix + g` 的 footer（`enter switch / search b/w/i/d/a states j/k/↑↓ move esc close`）沒寫出來的一個鍵：

> **`Space` = 切換游標所在 space 的展開/收起**

只在游標停在 **space 那一行**時有效（停在 tab/pane 行沒反應）。原始碼：v0.7.2 `src/app/input/modal.rs:273` → `toggle_selected_navigator_workspace_from()`（`src/app/actions.rs:649`）。你截圖裡前四個 space 是 `▸` 收起狀態，應該就是這樣按出來的。

但有三個限制，讓它沒辦法當「全部收起」用：

1. **每次開 `prefix+g` 都重置成全展開** — `open_navigator_from()` 會 `expanded_workspaces.clear()` 然後把所有 workspace 全塞回去（`actions.rs:356-360`）。收起狀態不跨次保存。
2. **一有搜尋字串或 `b`/`w`/`i`/`d` 狀態過濾就強制全展開** — `expanded = query_kind != Empty || …`（`actions.rs:400`）。只有 `a`（全部）或空查詢時收起才生效。
3. 這個收起狀態跟 **sidebar 的 `collapsed_space_keys` 是兩套獨立的**（sidebar 那套會寫進 `~/.config/herdr/session.json`，navigator 這套不會）。

上游都有人提過、都沒進：[#1256 goto_depth 設定（只顯示 space/tab、隱藏 pane）](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1256)、[#1255 vim 式 `h`/`l` 展開收合](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1255) —— 兩個都被 bot 以「issue 只收 bug，feature 去 discussions」關掉，轉到 [discussion #1248](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1248)。所以短期內不會有原生的 collapse-all。

## 3. 想「一目瞭然最 high-level 的 spaces」→ 用 `prefix + T`

那個 tv channel 本來就是扁平的 space-only 清單，等於一個**永久 collapse-all 視圖**，而且有 preview pane 顯示該 space 的細節。現在你這台跑起來長這樣：

```
w3   ~                       (10p, 10t)
w5   Agent Skill             (7p, 7t)
wP   chezmoi                 (6p, 6t)
wQ   atp-sipui               (6p, 5t)
wR   SmartHome               (6p, 6t)
…
```

次選是 `prefix + w`（原生 sidebar navigate mode，也是 space 層），但它沒有模糊搜尋。

```text
## Keybindings

Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.

> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.

| Key | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |

> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
| `prefix + M` | btop system monitor | command pane |
| `prefix + N` | nvtop GPU monitor | command pane |
| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
| `` prefix + u `` | **URL picker** — fzf-pick a URL from the pane and open it (`x open`); tmux-fzf-url analog. `--source recent` = full scrollback | command pane |
| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
| `prefix + P` | copy focused pane's **process info** to the clipboard | command pane |
| `prefix + D` | copy focused pane's **coordinate** (session>space>tab>pane) | command pane |
| `prefix + V` | copy focused pane's **content** (visible screen) | command pane |
| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
| `` prefix + p `` | **copy a file path** from the pane — two-tier fzf (paths that exist under the pane cwd on top), copies the resolved absolute path (`x copy`) | command pane |
| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |

## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot`)

Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.

=== pitfalls index ===
# Pitfalls

Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## Pitfalls vs the rest

This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:

| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |

A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.

## When to add a pitfall doc

Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:

- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
```

93:Live handoff is for update and remote attach flows that need to replace a running Herdr server. It asks the old server to transfer live panes to the new server, so pane processes can keep running across the server replacement.
94-
95:This is different from snapshot restore, pane history replay, and native agent session restore. Handoff tries to keep the current processes alive. The others reconstruct state after the old server has already stopped.
96-
97:Handoff protects long-lived server-owned session state: pane PTYs and processes, agent identity and durable metadata, and plugin/session state needed by the replacement server. It does not preserve transient coordination across the replacement boundary. In-flight CLI or API requests, waits, subscription streams, client sockets, and pane-to-pane messages may be interrupted; clients should reconnect and retry them.

107-
108:`herdr update --handoff` only applies to installs managed by Herdr's own updater. Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs are updated through their package managers, so `herdr update` is disabled there and cannot perform live handoff.

# herdr CLI dies with `protocol_mismatch` after `brew upgrade herdr` — and Homebrew installs cannot live-handoff

## Symptoms

Right after `brew upgrade herdr` on macOS, **every** `herdr` CLI call fails while the
UI you are sitting in keeps working perfectly:

\```console
$ herdr workspace list
{"id":"cli:workspace:list","error":{"code":"protocol_mismatch",
 "message":"client protocol 17 is newer than server protocol 16; restart the Herdr server
 before using this command. Stop the old server to use the new version.\nStopping exits pane
 processes.\nRun `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/Users/you/.config/herdr/herdr.sock herdr server stop`,
 then restart Herdr with the same socket override."}}
\```

Note the exit code is **0** — the error is in the JSON body, not the process status, so
naive `cmd || fallback` wrappers do not notice.

\```console
$ herdr status
client:
  version: 0.7.5
  protocol: 17
server:
  status: running
  version: 0.7.2
  protocol: 16
  compatible: no
update:
  restart_needed: yes
\```

Downstream, in this repo, that means the following silently stop working (usually as an
**empty picker** rather than an error, because the tv channels pipe through `jq` and
swallow stderr with `2>/dev/null`):

- `prefix + T` → `tv herdr-sesh`, `prefix + a` → `tv herdr-agent-panes`, `prefix + i` → `tv herdr-review`
- `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`)
- every `[[keys.command]]` helper that calls the CLI: `review-mark.sh`, `pane-copy.sh`,
  `path-pick.sh`, `url-pick.sh`, `new-tab-at-space-root.sh`

The herdr TUI itself is unaffected — the running server and its attached client are both
still the old binary, talking the old protocol to each other.

## Root cause

herdr's client↔server socket API is versioned by an integer `protocol`. A brew upgrade
swaps `/usr/local/bin/herdr` (→ `../Cellar/herdr/<new>/bin/herdr`) but **cannot restart the
running server** — so the new CLI (protocol 17) refuses to talk to the old server
(protocol 16). herdr fails closed here on purpose rather than risk a mismatched wire format.

The trap is the recovery path, not the diagnosis:

> **`herdr update --handoff` — the live, pane-preserving upgrade — is disabled on Homebrew,
> mise, and Nix installs.** Upstream: *"`herdr update --handoff` only applies to installs
> managed by Herdr's own updater. Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs are updated through their
> package managers, so `herdr update` is disabled there and cannot perform live handoff."*
> ([session-state docs](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/session-state.mdx))

So on **macOS (this repo installs herdr via homebrew-core)** there is **no** way to pick up a
new herdr version without stopping the server, and stopping the server **kills every pane
process** — shells, dev servers, tests, and every running coding agent.

Linux hosts are the opposite case: this repo installs the self-managed GitHub-release binary
into `~/.local/bin/herdr`, so `herdr update --handoff` *is* available there.

## Fix / workaround

There is no way to un-stage the upgrade short of `brew install herdr@<old>` (no such
formula exists). Pick one:

**A. Stay on the old server until a natural restart point.** The mismatch is CLI-only. Keep
using the TUI (`prefix+g` navigator, splits, tabs all still work — they are server-internal),
just avoid the CLI-backed helpers above. Restart at the end of the day.

**B. Restart deliberately, leaning on herdr's own restore.** Before stopping, know what
survives:

| Layer | Survives `herdr server stop`? |
|---|---|
| Workspace / tab / pane **topology** + labels | Yes — snapshot in `~/.config/herdr/session.json` |
| Pane **screen history** | Yes, if `[session]` history saving is on |
| AI-agent **conversations** | Yes, for agents with `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks + `resume_agents_on_restore = true` |
| **Running processes** (shells, servers, tests, `just`, builds) | **No — all killed** |

\```bash
HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$HOME/.config/herdr/herdr.sock" herdr server stop
herdr    # reattach; topology + agent sessions restore
\```

**C. Prevent it up front** — pin herdr out of blanket brew upgrades if a long-running
session matters more than being current:

\```bash
brew pin herdr        # `just upgrade-brew` / `brew upgrade` then skips it
brew unpin herdr      # when you're ready to take the restart
\```

## Why this is easy to misdiagnose

- The UI keeps working flawlessly, so nothing *feels* broken — only the side-channel
  helpers stop responding, and they mostly fail as empty pickers.
- `herdr --version` reports **0.7.5** (the new client binary) even though the server you are
  actually sitting inside is still **0.7.2**. Always cross-check with `herdr status`, which
  prints client and server separately plus `compatible:` / `restart_needed:`.
- The CLI exits **0** on `protocol_mismatch`; only the JSON body carries the failure.

## See also

- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) — install / upgrade / config-overlay model
- Upstream session-state + live-handoff doc: <https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/session-state.mdx>

```

+### Session navigator (`prefix + g`) — in-popup keys {#navigator-keys}
+
+The navigator is herdr's Cmd-K analog: a `space → tab → pane` tree with fuzzy search and agent-state filters. Its footer only advertises `enter switch · / search · b/w/i/d/a states · j/k/↑↓ move · esc close`, but several keys are live and **undocumented upstream** (verified against herdr 0.7.5 `src/app/input/modal.rs`):
+
+| Key | Effect |
+|---|---|
+| `space` | **toggle expand/collapse of the highlighted space** — fires only on a *space* row; silently no-ops on tab/pane rows |
+| `ctrl + d` / `ctrl + u` | half-page down / up |
+| `home` / `end` (or `G`) | first / last row |
+| `backspace` | drop an active state filter (`b`/`w`/`i`/`d`) back to all |
+| `a` | clear the query **and** the state filter |
+| `esc` | closes the popup immediately (on ≤ 0.7.2 it cleared query + filter first and only closed on a second press) |
+
+**Three limits that stop `space` from acting as a collapse-all** (`src/app/actions.rs`):
+
+1. **Every open resets to fully expanded** — `open_navigator_from()` clears `expanded_workspaces` then re-inserts every workspace. Collapse state does not survive closing the popup.
+2. **Any search query or `b`/`w`/`i`/`d` filter force-expands everything** (`expanded = query_kind != Empty || …`). Collapsing only has a visible effect under `a` / empty query.
+3. **The navigator's expand set is separate from the sidebar's** `collapsed_space_keys` — the latter is what `~/.config/herdr/session.json` persists, driven by the sidebar's right-click `Expand` / `Close group` menu. Collapsing a space in one does not affect the other.
+
+There is **no expand-all / collapse-all and no depth cap**. Upstream asks for both were closed unactioned under the issue-template policy (issues are bug-only): [#1256](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1256) (`ui.goto_depth = "workspace" | "tab" | "pane"`) and [#1255](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1255) (vim `h`/`l` to collapse/expand) → [discussion #1248](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1248).
+
+> **For a spaces-only overview, reach for `prefix + T`** (`tv herdr-sesh`) instead. It is a flat workspace list by construction — a permanent collapse-all view — and it can additionally *create* a space from a zoxide frecency dir, which the native navigator cannot. `prefix + w` is the other space-level option (native sidebar navigate mode) but has no fuzzy search.
+
 ## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot`)
 
 Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.

advertises and upstream never documented — most usefully `space` to
collapse/expand the highlighted space. Document the full set, verified
against herdr 0.7.5 `src/app/input/modal.rs`, plus the three reasons it
can't stand in for a collapse-all: every open resets to fully expanded,
any query/state filter force-expands, and the navigator's expand set is
independent of the sidebar's persisted `collapsed_space_keys`. Point
readers at `prefix+T` (`tv herdr-sesh`) for a spaces-only overview.

Also record the trap that surfaced while upgrading 0.7.2 -> 0.7.5: brew
swaps the binary but can't restart the server, so every CLI call fails
`protocol_mismatch` (exit 0, error in the JSON body) while the TUI keeps
working — which quietly empties every `tv herdr-*` channel and no-ops the
`[[keys.command]]` helpers. The kicker is that `herdr update --handoff`,
the pane-preserving path, is disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs, so
macOS has no way to take a new version without killing pane processes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

4	#
5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane custom-status metadata (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source
7	# review --custom-status …`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why custom-status and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. Verified: a
14	# pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so
15	# peeking into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
19	# surfaces the `custom_status` field, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO
20	# --json flag) lets the `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No
21	# sidecar file.
22	#
23	# Usage:
24	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
25	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
26	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
27	#
28	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
29	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
30	# focus_clear action. Keep the marker MATCH substring ("REVIEW") in sync with
31	# that channel's jq filter (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml).
32	set -eu
33	
34	SOURCE_ID='review'
35	MATCH='REVIEW'                 # substring the tv channel filters on (glyph-agnostic)
36	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
37	
38	usage() {
39	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
40	    exit 64
41	}
42	
43	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
44	
45	action="${1:-}"
46	pane="${2:-}"
47	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
48	
49	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
50	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
51	
52	_set() {
53	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --custom-status "$status" >/dev/null
54	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
55	}
56	
57	_clear() {
58	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-custom-status >/dev/null
59	    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
60	}
61	
62	case "$action" in
63	    set)   _set ;;
64	    clear) _clear ;;
65	    toggle)
66	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
67	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
68	            | jq -r '.result.pane.custom_status // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
69	        case "$current" in
70	            *"$MATCH"*) _clear ;;
71	            *)          _set ;;
72	        esac ;;
73	    *) usage ;;

是升級造成的，但**跟剛才那個 protocol mismatch 是兩回事** —— 這個更嚴重，因為重啟 server 也修不好。

## 診斷

0.7.4 把 `--custom-status` 整組換掉了，改成通用的**具名 token**：

| | ≤ 0.7.3 | ≥ 0.7.4 |
|---|---|---|
| 設定 | `--custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"` | `--token review="⭐ REVIEW"` |
| 清除 | `--clear-custom-status` | `--clear-token review` |
| 讀取 | `.result.pane.custom_status`（單一字串） | `.result.pane.tokens`（`{name: value}` map，上限 32） |
| 顯示 | sidebar **自動**渲染 | **不會自動顯示** —— 要在 row layout 裡引用 |

`herdr pane report-metadata --help` 現在只剩 `--token <NAME=VALUE>` / `--clear-token <NAME>`，`--custom-status` 完全不存在。

兩個值得記的點：

1. **changelog 沒把它列為 Breaking Change** —— 它藏在 0.7.4 的「### Added」裡：*"configurable row layouts … including built-in display tokens, per-agent overrides, custom metadata tokens"*。移除是靜默的。
2. 這就是為什麼錯誤長得不一樣：參數解析在 client 端先失敗，所以你看到 `unknown --custom-status` 而不是 `protocol_mismatch`。

## 影響範圍：6 個檔案

`executable_review-mark.sh`（3 個呼叫點 + toggle 的 jq 讀取）、`herdr-review.toml`（jq filter）、`24_herdr.sh`（`hmark`/`hunmark` 說明）、`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`、`docs/tools/herdr.{md,zh-TW.md}`（含可行性對照表）、`docs/shells/aliases.md`。另外 `backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md` 整份設計都建立在 `--custom-status` 上。

**順帶一個好消息**：那份 backlog 記的「`custom_status` 每 pane 只有單值，review 旗標會跟用量 driver 搶同一個欄位」的 caveat，在 token 模型下**自動消失**了 —— 各自用各自的 token name 就好。那個 backlog 反而被解鎖了。

12	# granularity — enough with one agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
13	#
14	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) via jq,
15	# filtered to panes whose custom_status contains "REVIEW" (glyph-agnostic; keep
16	# in sync with the MATCH substring in review-mark.sh):
17	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
18	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
19	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
20	#   3. custom_status  (⭐ REVIEW)
21	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
22	
23	[metadata]
24	name = "herdr-review"
25	description = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐) — jump to sessions you flagged for later"
26	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]
27	
28	[source]
29	command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select(.custom_status? // "" | test("REVIEW")) | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.custom_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
30	display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:3}  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
31	output = "{split:\t:0}"
32	
33	[preview]
34	command = '''
35	pane='{split:\t:0}'
36	printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
37	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
38	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
39	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
40	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
41	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
42	'''
43	
44	[ui]
45	input_header = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐)"
46	
47	[ui.preview_panel]
48	size = 60
49	
50	[keybindings]
51	enter = "actions:focus"
52	alt-t = "actions:focus"
53	alt-c = ["actions:focus_clear", "reload_source"]
54	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
55	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
56	
57	[actions.focus]
58	description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab (keep the ⭐)"
59	command = '''
60	ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
61	[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
62	[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
63	'''
64	mode = "fork"
65	
66	[actions.focus_clear]
67	description = "Jump to the pane AND clear the ⭐ (mark read)"
68	command = '''
69	pane='{split:\t:0}'; ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
70	[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
71	[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
72	[ -n "$pane" ] && "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh" clear "$pane" >/dev/null 2>&1
73	'''
74	mode = "fork"
75	
76	[actions.copy_id]
77	description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
78	command = '''
79	d='{split:\t:0}'
80	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
81	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
82	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
83	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
84	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
85	fi
86	'''
87	mode = "fork"
88	
89	[actions.copy_dir]
90	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
91	command = '''
92	d='{split:\t:4}'
93	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
94	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
95	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
96	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
97	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
98	fi
99	'''
100	mode = "fork"
101

# ── Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ───────────────────────────────────
# hmark/hunmark toggle a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag via herdr's
# custom-status metadata — ORTHOGONAL to agent state, so peeking into a done pane
# (which flips it to idle) does NOT clear the flag. The mark logic lives in
# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh (dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh);
# these are thin CLI wrappers defaulting the pane to the ambient HERDR_PANE_ID.
# The prefix+m keybind and the `tv herdr-review` inbox share that same script.
_herdr_review_script="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh"

# hmark [PANE] — flag a pane for later review (default: current pane).
function herdr-mark() {
    case "${1:-}" in
        -h|--help)
            cat <<'EOF'
hmark — flag a herdr pane as "review-pending" (⭐), analog of tmux bookmark

Usage: hmark [PANE_ID]

With no PANE_ID, flags the CURRENT pane (ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID). The flag is a
herdr custom-status, orthogonal to agent state — it survives the pane going idle
when you peek in. Clear with `hunmark`, toggle with prefix+m, list flagged panes
with `tv herdr-review` (prefix+i inside herdr).
EOF
            return 0 ;;
    esac
    local pane="${1:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}"
    [ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "hmark: no pane id (not inside herdr?). Pass one: hmark w1:p1" >&2; return 1; }
    "$_herdr_review_script" set "$pane"
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-26 11:22:48Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read EN review-pending flag section

`sed -n '287,320p' docs/tools/herdr.md`

```text
The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.

The fix uses herdr's **per-pane custom-status metadata**, which is orthogonal to native agent detection:

```bash
herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"   # set (persistent — no --ttl-ms)
herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-custom-status         # clear
```

Verified: a pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `custom_status` field and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth.

Surfaces (all sharing one script, `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh` — the analog of tmux's `toggle-bookmark.sh`):

| Surface | Action |
|---|---|
| `hmark` / `hunmark` (aliases in `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`) | set / clear on the current pane (ambient `$HERDR_PANE_ID`), or pass a pane id |
| `prefix+m` | toggle the flag on the focused pane (uses `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`) |
| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | the **inbox**: lists only flagged panes. `Enter` focuses & **keeps** the ⭐ (you may still be mid-review); `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read") |

**Caveat — `custom_status` is a single value per pane.** The deferred usage-status driver (below) also pushes `--custom-status`; although it uses a different `--source`, `herdr pane get` exposes one flattened `custom_status`, so the two would contend for the visible label. No live conflict today (the usage driver isn't built and review flags are short-lived), but see [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).

## Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (`prefix+P/D/V/S`)

Four one-keypress "grab this pane onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.

| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |

The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
```

Enter focuses the pane's workspace/tab and **keeps** the flag; `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read"). Bound to `prefix+i`. See the **Review-pending flag** section below.
298:> **herdr ≥ 0.7.4 only, and the token needs a row layout to be visible.** 0.7.4 replaced `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field with this namespaced token map — a silent removal, not listed as a breaking change. Two consequences: on older herdr the helper dies with `unknown --custom-status`, and unlike `custom_status` a token is rendered **only** where a sidebar row layout names it. That is why `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` pins `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` with `"$review"` appended to herdr's default first row — drop that and the flag still works through `prefix+i`, but the ⭐ disappears from the sidebar. See [`pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md).
358:herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses — note both write the single per-pane `custom_status`). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
364:- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via per-pane `custom_status` metadata; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*

```text
tmux 那邊有逐視窗書籤（`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`,靠 `#{?@bookmark_status,…}` 渲染）。herdr **沒有 `#{@option}` 狀態列插值**,所以那套機制不能直接移植——但這裡真正重要的用途可以:**「agent 跑完了（`done`）但我還沒 review」**。herdr 一旦你點進去瞄一眼就把 `done` pane 塌成 `idle`,唯一還需要注意的訊號就此消失。

解法用 herdr 的**逐 pane custom-status metadata**,它與原生 agent 偵測正交:

```bash
herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"   # 設定（永久——不帶 --ttl-ms）
herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-custom-status         # 清除
```

已驗證:一個 pane 可以同時帶 `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` 與 `agent_status:"idle"`——所以點進去**不會**清掉旗標（重點所在）。`herdr pane get` 會吐出 `custom_status` 欄位,`herdr pane list`（原生 JSON——**不**加 `--json` flag）讓收件匣列舉被標記的 pane,所以**不需要 sidecar 檔**;herdr 自己就是真相源。

各介面（共用同一支腳本 `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh`,即 tmux `toggle-bookmark.sh` 的對應物）:

| 介面 | 動作 |
|---|---|
| `hmark` / `hunmark`（`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` 的 alias） | 對目前 pane（環境值 `$HERDR_PANE_ID`）set / clear,或傳入 pane id |
| `prefix+m` | 切換 focus pane 的旗標（用 `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`） |
| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | **收件匣**:只列出被標記的 pane。`Enter` focus 過去並**保留** ⭐（你可能還在 review 中）;`Alt+C` focus **並**清除（「mark read」） |

**Caveat——`custom_status` 每 pane 單值。** 延後中的用量狀態 driver（下方）也會推 `--custom-status`;雖然用不同 `--source`,`herdr pane get` 只吐一個扁平的 `custom_status`,兩者會爭同一個可見標籤。目前無實際衝突（driver 未建、review 旗標短暫）,但見 [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md)。

```text
Decision at research time: **keep CodexBar as the primary usage view; do not install a herdr plugin now.** Backlog a DIY driver for when the user lives in herdr full-time and wants Claude+Codex quota in the sidebar without alt-tabbing to the menu bar.

## The hook (verified)

herdr can render arbitrary status TEXT next to a pane/agent in the sidebar via the metadata API:

```
herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source <id> --custom-status "Claude 62% • Codex 78%5h" --ttl-ms <n>
```

`--custom-status` + `--ttl-ms` (auto-expiry) is exactly the driver surface — a background timer computes the string and pushes it per pane. (`herdr pane report-agent … --custom-status` is the other entry point.) No core/config change required.

> **⚠ Shared field with the review-pending flag (shipped 2026-07).** `custom_status` is a **single value per pane**. The review-pending flag (`hmark` / `prefix+m` / `tv herdr-review`, script `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh`, `--source review`) already writes `custom_status`. Although this driver would use a different `--source`, `herdr pane get` exposes only ONE flattened `custom_status`, so the two producers contend for the visible label (last-writer / internal priority). When this driver is built, decide the interaction explicitly — e.g. compose both into one string, give the review ⭐ priority when set, or move one producer to `--title` / `--state-label` instead of `--custom-status`.

## Prior art (herdr plugins)

- **[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)** — closest analog to CodexBar's *Codex* provider. Reads local Codex JSONL at `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (default `~/.codex/sessions`), finds the newest `rate_limits` event, publishes a compact `"78%5h 64%wk"` label into the agents sidebar via a background service, plus a `codex-usage-watch` refreshing pane. **Same on-disk source CodexBar uses for Codex; no OpenAI API call.** Codex-ONLY.
- **[Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard](https://github.com/Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard)** — per-agent token/cost TUI pane (Pi session JSONL + OpenCode server API). Token/cost, not subscription quota.
- **Gap**: no herdr plugin covers **Claude / ChatGPT** subscription quota. CodexBar gets those from OAuth/cookies/CLI, which nothing in the herdr ecosystem mirrors.

## Options when this is picked up

- **A — install the Codex-only plugin** (Effort S): add `herdr plugin install jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit` to the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block pattern in `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (idempotent, mirrors how `cloudmanic/herdr-plus` is installed). Gets Codex quota in the sidebar. Update `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` A–Z + `docs/tools/herdr.md`. **Leaves Claude/ChatGPT uncovered.**
- **B — DIY driver** (Effort M): a small background loop (shell or uv script) that computes `"Claude X% • Codex Y%"` and calls `herdr pane report-metadata … --custom-status` for each agent pane. Data sources, cheapest first:
  1. Reuse **CodexBar's own cached data** — CodexBar reads `~/.codex` (rate_limits) and `~/.claude`; if it caches to `~/.config/codexbar/` or similar, read that instead of re-deriving. (Verify what CodexBar persists; it's a mix of local files + OAuth/cookies/Keychain.)
  2. Codex: read `~/.codex/sessions` rate_limits directly (same as the plugin).
  3. Claude: `~/.claude` usage files if present; else scrape the Claude CLI. Hardest part; may not be cleanly file-derivable.
  - Wire the loop as a herdr `[[keys.command]]` `type="shell"` (detached) entry in `dot_config/herdr/create_config.toml`, or a pueue/launchd timer. Keep the per-pane `--source` stable so labels update in place.

## Open questions

```md
# `unknown --custom-status` — herdr 0.7.4 silently replaced custom-status with metadata tokens

## Symptoms

After upgrading herdr (0.7.3 → 0.7.4 or later), the review-pending ⭐ stops working:

\```console
$ herdr pane report-metadata w1:p1 --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"
error: unexpected argument '--custom-status' found
\```

Concretely, in this repo:

- `prefix + m` (toggle review flag) and `hmark` / `hunmark` die with the above.
- `tv herdr-review` / `prefix + i` opens **empty** — the channel's jq filter reads a
  `custom_status` field that no longer exists, so it matches nothing and reports no error.
- Any ⭐ set before the upgrade vanishes from the sidebar.

Distinguishing it from [the other herdr upgrade trap](herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md):
this one fails during **client-side argument parsing**, so you get `unexpected argument`
rather than `protocol_mismatch`, and **restarting the server does not fix it**.

## Root cause

herdr 0.7.4 replaced the single free-text custom-status with a namespaced **metadata token
map**:

| | ≤ 0.7.3 | ≥ 0.7.4 |
|---|---|---|
| set | `--custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"` | `--token review="⭐ REVIEW"` |
| clear | `--clear-custom-status` | `--clear-token review` |
| read | `.result.pane.custom_status` (string) | `.result.pane.tokens` (`{name: value}` map, ≤ 32 entries, names `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$`) |
| render | automatic in the sidebar | **only** where a row layout names `$<token>` |

**The removal is not listed as a breaking change.** It is folded into a 0.7.4 *"### Added"*
bullet — *"configurable row layouts for expanded Space and Agent sidebar entries, including
built-in display tokens, per-agent overrides, custom metadata tokens, and pane/workspace
metadata reporting through the CLI and socket API"* — with no deprecation notice and no
mention of `custom_status` anywhere in the changelog. Nothing warns you before the CLI
rejects the flag.

## Fix

Three names must move together — that is the whole migration:

1. **`dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh`** — `TOKEN='review'`; `--token "$TOKEN=$status"`,
   `--clear-token "$TOKEN"`, and read with `jq -r --arg t "$TOKEN" '.result.pane.tokens[$t] // ""'`.
   Presence of the token is now the flag, so the old `MATCH='REVIEW'` substring test is gone.
2. **`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml`** — `select((.tokens.review? // "") != "")`
   and emit `.tokens.review`.
3. **`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`** — the part that is easy to miss:

\```toml
[ui.sidebar.agents]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
  ["agent"],
]
\```

Without step 3 the flag *works* (the API stores it, `prefix+i` lists it) but is **invisible in
the sidebar**, because tokens — unlike `custom_status` — are only rendered where a row layout
references them. herdr's own default is `[["state_icon", "workspace", "tab"], ["agent"]]`;
we append `$review` to the first row.

Validate before applying — `herdr config check` is client-local, so it works even while a
stale server is running:

\```bash
chezmoi execute-template < .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml > /tmp/h.toml
HERDR_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/h.toml herdr config check     # => "config: ok"
\```

It genuinely catches mistakes here — a misspelled key reports
`unknown config key ui.sidebar.agents.rowz; ignoring key`, and a bare (non-`$`) custom token
reports ``unknown sidebar token `foo`; custom tokens must start with `$` ``.

## Silver lining

`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md` was blocked on `custom_status` being one value per
pane — the deferred usage driver and the review ⭐ would have fought over the same visible
label. Namespaced tokens dissolve that: a `usage` token and a `review` token coexist. The
only carry-over is that both must be listed in the same `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` block.

## Pinning cost

Overriding `rows` means our managed `[ui]` table now pins herdr's sidebar layout — upstream
changes to the default rows will not reach us. Re-check the block against
`herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.

## See also

- [`herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server`](herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md) — the *other* breakage from the same upgrade (protocol mismatch)
- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) § Review-pending flag

```

fix(herdr): migrate review-pending ⭐ to 0.7.4 metadata tokens

herdr 0.7.4 removed `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field in
favour of a namespaced token map, so `prefix+m` and `hmark` died with
`unexpected argument '--custom-status'` and `tv herdr-review` opened
empty (its jq filter read a field that no longer exists, so it matched
nothing and reported nothing). Upstream folded the removal into a 0.7.4
"### Added" bullet about configurable sidebar row layouts — no breaking
change entry, no deprecation.

now presence-based so the old MATCH substring is gone), the
`.tokens.review` lookups in herdr-review.toml, and — the part that is
easy to miss — a pinned `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` carrying `$review`.
Unlike custom_status, a token renders ONLY where a row layout names it,
so without that block the flag works but is invisible in the sidebar.
The cost is that our managed [ui] table now pins herdr's sidebar layout.

Verified `herdr config check` on the rendered template ("config: ok"),
with controls proving it catches a misspelled key and a bare non-`$`
token; new jq filters exercised against fixtures covering absent,
empty-map, empty-value and foreign-token panes.

Also unblocks backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md: its blocking caveat
was that custom_status is one value per pane, so the usage driver and
the review ⭐ would contend for the label. Namespaced tokens dissolve
that — only constraint left is sharing the one rows block.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

```text
# Pre-commit hooks for dotfiles repository
# See https://pre-commit.com for more information
# Run `just pre-commit-setup` to install hooks

repos:
  # Auto-redact secrets in agent artifacts (specstory history + coding-agent
  # plan dirs) BEFORE gitleaks runs. If the script rewrites any file,
  # pre-commit reports "files were modified by this hook" and the user must
  # `git add` + re-commit -- same UX as trailing-whitespace / end-of-file-fixer.
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: redact-agent-secrets
        name: Auto-redact secrets in agent artifacts
        entry: ./scripts/redact_secrets.py --fix
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        files: |
          (?x)
          ^(\.specstory/history|\.claude/plans|\.cursor/plans|\.cursor/rules|\.opencode/plans|\.specify|\.codex)/.*\.md$
          | ^raycast/.*\.json$

      # Single-source-of-truth guard: PROMPTS in dotfiles_init.py generates the
      # prompt block in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl and the ARG/RUN blocks in Dockerfile,
      # and is coverage-checked against the README table. Fail if any drifted
      # (fix with `just gen-prompts`). See scripts/init/README.md.
      - id: dotfiles-init-gen-check
        name: chezmoi prompts in sync (dotfiles_init.py gen --check)
        entry: uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check --source .
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        files: |
          (?x)
          ^scripts/init/dotfiles_init\.py$
          | ^\.chezmoi\.toml\.tmpl$
          | ^Dockerfile$
```
</details></tool-use>
